official.description: COMSTECH and prestigious CCoE member institutions jointly offer research fellowships to young women researchers, scientists and engineers in OIC countries to enable them to spend 6-12 months at a relevant centre of excellence. The purpose is to enhance the research and development capacity of promising women researchers and engineers from LDCs at the beginning of their research career, fostering linkages for further collaboration in their fields.
official.region: Least developed countries of the OIC (16 listed: 15 in Africa plus Afghanistan); hosted at designated centres of excellence in OIC member states
official.program_type: Research fellowship for research and advanced training, offered jointly by COMSTECH and CCoE member institutions

verification.notes: Official COMSTECH call page and its linked application form read in full on 2026-10-10; the page publishes benefits in kind only (COMSTECH bears international low-cost airfare; host institutions provide accommodation, subsistence, supervision and mentoring) with no monetary value, no tuition or enrolment-fee coverage and no English score stated anywhere.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a rolling, year-round call for a 6-12 month research placement at an OIC centre of excellence, so there is no deadline to miss but also no cash award value published anywhere: COMSTECH pays only international low-cost airfare, while accommodation, subsistence and mentoring come from the host institution. You apply through the COMSTECH online application form, list up to two preferred CCoE host institutions (placement is explicitly not guaranteed), and are judged on scientific merit by COMSTECH together with the host institutions' Joint Scholarship Committee. Because tuition and enrolment fees are never mentioned, treat degree fees as your own cost and budget for visa, insurance and personal expenses on top.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career women scientists and engineers from the 16 listed OIC least-developed countries (15 of them in Africa) who hold at least an M.S. (a Ph.D. for post-graduate placements), are inside the 35/45 age caps, and can commit six to twelve months to a host laboratory in another OIC country.
application_readiness_checklist: Check that your passport expiry comfortably covers the full 6-12 month placement plus visa processing, because the form asks for the passport number and expiry date.
Pre-compress every upload to the published limits before you start: scans in .pdf or .jpg under 300kb and the CV as a .pdf under 500kb, since oversized files block the submission.
Arrange a fresh photograph taken within the last six months for the CV; the form requires the picture to be recent.
Request a recommendation letter from your current or most recent institution early - you need exactly one scan, and supervisor turnaround is the usual bottleneck.
Choose two CCoE member institutions whose labs genuinely match your research objectives before writing the form, since preferences are considered but never guaranteed.
Draft the two 200-word statements separately - motivation/fit, then concrete research or training objectives - because the form enforces a minimum length on both.
common_rejection_risks: Applying as an established researcher: the page states preference for young women scientists at the beginning of their research career, and the 35/45 age caps are hard limits for graduate and post-graduate study.
Naming a preferred host centre without evidence your proposal fits that centre's work - with placement not guaranteed, a weak candidate-lab match is an easy filter-out.
Upload failures: degree/transcript, passport and recommendation scans must be .pdf or .jpg under 300kb and the CV .pdf under 500kb; oversized or wrongly formatted files are a paperwork rejection.
Under-length motivation or research-objective statements (the form demands at least 200 words each), which reads as low effort on a merit-based call.
Form details that do not match the passport scan, or a passport expiring inside the fellowship window.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: No cash amounts are published at all. Beyond the low-cost airfare and host-provided accommodation and subsistence, expect to fund visa fees, health insurance, local transport, personal expenses, any enrolment or tuition fees (none are covered), and the difference between the offered low-cost fare and a fare you would actually prefer to fly.
document_audit: Form answers must be given exactly as per passport (name, date of birth, passport number, expiry) and must match the passport scan.
Degree/transcript and passport scans: .pdf or .jpg only, maximum 300kb each - many phone photos exceed this and need compressing.
CV: .pdf only, maximum 500kb, must enlist all educational/professional activities and research publications, and carry a photograph less than six months old.
Only one recommendation letter is accepted, and it must come from your current or most recent institution.
The form also asks for previous visits abroad, employment history, marital status, number of children, religion, and medical declarations - incomplete answers stall the review.
alerts: Rolling intake means you can apply any time, but it also means there is no guarantee a suitable slot will be free at your preferred host centre when your file is reviewed.
The fellowship is extendable only upon recommendation of the host institution, so the initial award and any extension are two separate judgement calls.
Airfare support is explicitly low-cost international airfare only - upgrades, excess baggage and preferred routings are on you.
Nothing on the official page mentions tuition or enrolment-fee support, and no monetary award value is published; treat any stipend figure seen on unaffiliated sites as unverified.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the online COMSTECH application form linked from the call page with all scans attached; applications and nominations are accepted year-round, and COMSTECH decides jointly with the host institutions' Joint Scholarship Committee on scientific merit.
